001: Haoran, you just joined our department. How are you settling in?
Overall it's great, it's just that everyone talks so fast in meetings, and I'm having a hard time keeping up.
We're used to getting straight to the point. Take your time, no need to rush.
Got it. From now on, I'll prepare the materials in advance to keep up with everyone's pace.
Right, that'll make things much more efficient. Feel free to ask me anytime if you have questions.
Okay, thank you. I'll adapt as quickly as I can.
002: Jingyi, how do you think our company's atmosphere compares to your last one?
The biggest difference I feel is that here, there's a strong emphasis on teamwork, not so much on individual heroics.
Yeah, we value collective results more. The credit goes to everyone.
That's great. At my old company, people were always taking credit for others' work, and it wore everyone out.
Our culture here is about supporting each other. You'll come to see that more and more.
Mm, I can already feel it. Everyone is really willing to help.
003: Tianyou, are you going to the department dinner next week?
Of course I'll go. I heard it's a tradition for our team.
Right, we do it once a month. It's mainly to relax and bond with each other.
That's great. I want to take this chance to get to know the other colleagues better.
Just remember, no talking about work. Everyone just chats and jokes around.
Haha, got it. I'll definitely be mindful of that.
004: Jiaqi, do you think our company's dress code is strict?
I think it's pretty relaxed. As long as you're not too casual, it's fine.
Yeah, except when we meet clients, just dressing comfortably and appropriately is fine.
That's great. My last company required formal business attire, and I really couldn't get used to it.
We care more about work results, not so much about those outward formalities.
I really like this kind of culture. It feels a bit freer.
005: Zixuan, have you noticed that before meetings, people in our department like to chat a bit?
Yeah, I've noticed. It seems like they warm up the atmosphere before getting down to business.
It's one of our habits. It helps keep meetings from feeling too tense.
I think it's nice. When everyone's in a relaxed mood, discussions go more smoothly.
Right. If there's something you'd like to talk about, you can also start the conversation yourself.
Okay, I'll give it a try next time and try to fit in with everyone.
006: Yuxuan, what do you think of our company's overtime culture?
From what I've observed, it seems like nobody really advocates for pointless overtime.
Exactly. We value efficiency. Once the work is done, we leave on time.
That's different from a lot of companies. I think it's really rare.
But when a project is tight, everyone does stay late voluntarily.
Of course. At critical moments, we definitely have to stick it out together. I totally understand.
007: Junjie, what do you think of our leader's management style?
I feel like he gives us a lot of autonomy. He leaves plenty of room for us to work on our own.
Right. He cares more about results and usually doesn't interfere too much in the process.
I adapt well to this style. It makes me more motivated to work.
But just remember to report your progress regularly so he's kept in the loop.
Okay, I'll make sure to keep him updated so he doesn't have to worry.
008: Tingting, I've noticed our company really encourages cross-department communication. Have you noticed that?
Yeah, I have. When people have questions, they go straight to the right person. No beating around the bush.
Right. We don't put much emphasis on hierarchy. Even peers can give direct feedback to each other.
That really does make things more efficient. It saves a lot of trouble from relaying messages through middlemen.
Yeah, as long as it's good for the work, anyone can offer suggestions.
I really like this open atmosphere. It feels very transparent.
009: Haoran, have you gotten used to our company's email communication habits?
Pretty much. It's just that I've noticed everyone replies really quickly.
We have an unwritten rule: work emails should be replied to on the same day whenever possible.
That's a good habit. It prevents a lot of things from being delayed.
Right. And for important matters, you should always CC the relevant people and keep a record.
Got it. I'll pay attention to those details so I don't make mistakes.
010: Jingyi, what do you think of our company's training system?
I think it's quite comprehensive. New hires even get a dedicated mentor.
Yeah, the company really values talent development and is willing to invest time in it.
That gives me a real sense of security. I feel like I can learn a lot here.
Study hard. The company hopes to cultivate key members of the team.
I'll do my best and hope to become independent as soon as possible. I won't let anyone down.
